_about: Hand-kept inputs for AI Economy -> Build-Out, for things no API carries. Every value needs an as-of date and a source URL; never estimate. Rows with "example": true are ignored by the tracker. See docs/ai-tracker.md for how to add rows.

events.counterparty: Lender, SPV partner, vendor or investor
events.description: One sentence: what was agreed and why it matters for the funding question.

Google bought about $10.0B of Anthropic preferred stock in March 2026 and $10.0B more in the May 2026 Series H, with up to $20.0B more in notes or stock to 2030, while Anthropic committed at least about $114.5B to Google compute for April 2026 to July 2033.

Amazon bought about $5.0B of Anthropic preferred stock in April 2026 and $5.0B more in the May 2026 Series H, with up to $15.0B more released in $5.0B steps as compute capacity is delivered, while Anthropic committed at least $110.0B to AWS for May 2026 to April 2036.

Alongside about $161.2B of five-year TPU equipment leases, Broadcom (or a financial partner it assigns) will buy up to $42.0B of 9% paid-in-kind convertible notes whose only use is paying that lease rent: the supplier lends its customer the money to pay it.

The Broadcom TPU leases are signed by two special-purpose subsidiaries, consolidated and guaranteed by Anthropic and secured on the equipment, after a $2.5B cash deposit into escrow in April 2026 with up to $10.0B more possibly restricted.
AMD committed to buy up to $5.0B of Anthropic stock, released as its MI450 Helios systems are delivered and deployed from 2027, against more than $20B Anthropic expects to spend on that capacity.

events.counterparty: Data-center developers and a power counterparty
events.description: Anthropic guarantees up to $0.8B of developers' costs, including long-lead equipment, and up to $500M of a data-center provider's power purchase contract; the S-1 also says some partners guarantee Anthropic's own data-center leases, with no amount given.
